content.text: The summary component already has a signed category bar helper and currency grouped server totals. The new time series has to be derived from declaration entries because the API summary carries only first/last dates; its x-axis must explicitly say registration week. The sample has only GBP entries, with a known total of £2,323,720.45.

const r = await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/exposed-summary-design-luna.md <<'EOF' # Member summary redesign candidate ## Grounded model `EntityDetails.svelte` owns data loading and chooses `MemberIdentity` plus either `MemberSummary` or `MemberHistory`. The identity component sees only the `MemberProfile`; the summary owns the loaded `MemberDetails` and currently renders server totals and category bars. `entity-details.ts` parses API data to typed `MemberDetails`; `summary.currencies[]` contains exact decimal-string totals grouped by currency/category, while `declarations[]` contains category and nullable `registeredAt` plus each entry's exact decimal-string amount and nullable currency. Dates are validated as parseable strings, not normalized to dates. `formatAmount` formats exact decimal text without currency. Existing category bars use BigInt scaling, preserve sign and avoid `Number` money arithmetic. No chart dependency or chart component pattern appears in these files. Existing CSS draws category bars, but the summary spec already asserts these class structures and labels. The history UI filters declaration registration dates, so registration-time semantics are established in the UI. The profile header belongs to `MemberIdentity`, so placing a total at its upper right needs either a prop or a wrapper/layout change; adding it in `MemberSummary` would visually put it below the header and fail the request. ## Design Use one small pure view-model adapter in `entity-details.ts` to produce chart-ready values, keeping API parsing and all currency amounts as exact decimal strings. Give `MemberIdentity` the GBP `Total` (or a narrow `{amount, unknownAmountCount}` value), render that in a right-aligned header block. GBP formats as `£` plus the existing exact grouping; all other currencies retain their currency code. If no GBP total exists, show an unavailable/empty state, never a fabricated £0. Existing server summaries remain the source for lifetime and category totals. `MemberSummary` becomes a vertical summary: lifetime known value stays at the top of the summary content only if not promoted to the header; then category chart and weekly earnings chart; then recent declarations. Remove entry-count/context prose blocks (stored declaration count, entry counts, category intro). Keep data-quality notes needed to interpret partial or missing amounts. Currency grouping is retained: never combine different currencies into one monetary sum. For the supplied Nigel Farage record, all 124 entries are GBP, so the displayed total is `£2,323,720.45`. Prefer a focused SVG chart component over stretching CSS bars into a time-series chart. SVG supports a baseline, labels, varying weekly columns, negative bars, and a compact accessible description without adding a chart library. Keep chart input/output types and exact arithmetic in the domain adapter; SVG rendering stays presentational. Category chart may retain the existing horizontal proportional-bar presentation but format GBP amounts with £. Weekly graph aggregates only earnings category IDs 1 (ad hoc), 2 (ongoing), and 12 (legacy employment earnings); label it **Earnings by registration week**. The dates are `registeredAt`, not payment/earned dates. State this in the accessible title/caption and show a short visible sublabel such as “Grouped by declaration registration week.” Construct Monday UTC buckets from `registeredAt`: parse the ISO instant, take its UTC calendar date, then its Monday. Fill every Monday from the first to last dated earning entry so quiet weeks have a zero baseline. Preserve negative aggregate values below the baseline. Skip undated declarations and report the count; if there are no dated GBP earnings, render a clear empty message rather than an empty graph. Where any earnings amount/currency is unknown, plot the known subtotal and state that the weekly totals are partial; don't coerce unknown values to zero silently. Avoid JS `Number` for money; use a common decimal scale and BigInt for sum and bar scaling, converting only the final normalized geometry to a finite SVG coordinate. ## Example data check From `/tmp/exposed-member-5091.json`: - Known GBP lifetime amount: £2,323,720.45 (124 GBP entries). - Category 1, “Employment and earnings - Ad hoc payments”: £1,951,169.44 (101 entries). - Category 2, ongoing employment and earnings: £105,928.40 (3 entries). - Category 12 has no GBP entries in this snapshot. Earnings categories 1/2/12 therefore total £2,057,097.84. - Earnings series has 30 nonzero registered weeks across 2024-07-29 to 2026-09-14, from 104 entries; no earnings entries are undated. Fill intervening Mondays with zero. (All-declaration registration range is 2024-07-22 to 2026-09-17.) ## Suggested module surface In `frontend/src/lib/entity-details.ts`: ```ts export interface WeeklyAmount { week: string; // YYYY-MM-DD, Monday in UTC amount: string; // exact signed decimal; zero buckets included unknownAmountCount: number; } export interface EarningsSeries { currency: string; weeks: WeeklyAmount[]; undatedEntryCount: number; unknownAmountCount: number; } export function earningsByRegistrationWeek( declarations: MemberDeclaration[], currency: string, earningCategoryIds: ReadonlySet, ): EarningsSeries; export function formatCurrencyAmount(amount: string | null, currency: string): string; ``` An implementation may use a canonical `EARNING_CATEGORY_IDS` constant (`1, 2, 12`) next to the helper to avoid duplicating the vocabulary in component markup. Convert each external `registeredAt` to a validated UTC Monday at the aggregation boundary. If `week` remains a string for `Intl`, keep it canonical and parse it only in the chart formatter. Keep `currency` in API types and all funder consumers untouched. A component API can remain small: ```svelte ``` `EarningsByWeek` receives already aggregated exact values and renders inline `

` instead. Use accessible date tick labels and a currency-aware y-axis/tooltip or a list/table equivalent for exact value access. ## File scope and UX risks - `frontend/src/MemberIdentity.svelte`: accept the summary currency totals and align the known total at the upper right beside the name; wrap responsively. - `frontend/src/MemberSummary.svelte`: remove count/context blocks, format GBP with £, retain unknown-data notes, add earnings series component. - `frontend/src/EarningsByWeek.svelte` (new): accessible SVG and empty state only. - `frontend/src/lib/entity-details.ts`: exact weekly aggregation, currency formatter, canonical earnings category IDs; no change to transport fields/API or funder presentation. - `frontend/src/styles.css`: header alignment/wrap and SVG axis, baseline, positive/negative bars, sparse month ticks; remove obsolete summary layout styles. - `frontend/tests/entity-details.spec.ts`: adjust display expectations and add behavior coverage for Monday UTC grouping, skipped-week zeros, negative values, unknown amount/currency, and undated entries. Verify category summary uses server amounts and GBP prefix. Main risks: confusing registration date with income timing; missing zero weeks in a sparse series; treating unknown values as zero; losing sign below baseline; inaccessible SVG with a hover-only value; header overflow for long names or large totals; and accidentally changing currency behavior for funder details. Existing tests assert `.member-total`, `.signed-bar`, and count text, so update affected assertions rather than preserving summary scaffolding. No files in the repository were changed. ## Candidate rationale This candidate keeps data semantics and exact decimal arithmetic in the existing typed entity module and keeps SVG rendering as a narrow presentation component. An all-CSS graph would reuse current bars but makes time-axis labels, negative values, sparse buckets, and screen-reader descriptions awkward. A general chart package would add dependency surface for two simple charts. Inlining all aggregation in Svelte would shorten file count but mix money/date domain rules into markup and make edge cases harder to reason about. EOF",workdir:"/Users/jamie/development/exposed",max_output_tokens:100}); text(r.output)
